skeleton: chubby mother Triceratops standing on four stubby legs, three-quarter view turned to the left: root on the ground under the body; body (pivot at the hips' height under the middle) with belly squash, the body piece carrying the fluffy cream chest and the shoulders up under the head and frill (its top a soft unoutlined edge) and its back running to the root of the tail, ending in a soft unoutlined cut the tail tucks under; head with its big scalloped frill and three blunt horns at the neck (no neck of its own, its own jaw line), face with eyes (the far one smaller, by the nose horn), brows and mouth; legFF (far front) and legBF (far back) behind the body, shaded; legFN (near front) and legBN (near back) in front of the body, tops faded in; tail behind the body, its bone at the join; a fern sprig on its own bone at the mouth for munching.

sheets.prompt:
Image 1 is a sticker of a chubby orange Triceratops with darker orange spots, a fluffy cream chest, three soft blunt cream horns and a big round frill with soft scalloped bumps, standing on four stubby legs, turned a little to the left. Draw this exact Triceratops as a cut-out paper puppet: its separate body parts laid out on one sheet, the same drawing style, colours, texture, line and proportions as in image 1, every part at the size it has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, spread out over the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, no part touching or overlapping another:
1. the body: the round, chubby spotted body with its fluffy cream chest and cream tummy, turned as in image 1, without head, without frill, without legs and without tail: no legs, shoulders, thighs, haunches or feet drawn on it, its underside one smooth rounded line from the chest to the back. At the top front, the broad shoulders and the fluffy cream throat go straight up as wide as they are under the head in image 1, including what is normally hidden behind the head and the frill, and end in a soft, smooth edge with NO outline (it is hidden under the head). At the back, the spotted back runs on smoothly into the very root of the thick tail and ends there in a soft edge cut straight down, with NO outline across it (the tail tucks under it): no round bump, no stump, no line where the tail would join. The drawing's dark outline runs only along the front of the fluffy chest, under the tummy and along the back.
2. the head with its frill, as one piece: the big round head with its short rounded beak, its two little nostrils, its rosy cheek, its three soft blunt cream horns (the small one on the nose, the two big ones over the eyes) and the big round spotted frill behind it with its soft blunt scalloped bumps, turned as in image 1, the frill drawn whole including what is normally hidden; with a completely blank face: no eyes, no eyebrows, no mouth and no mouth line, the beak and the cream jaw one smooth shape; keep the nostrils and the rosy cheek. Its dark outline runs round the beak, under the jaw and the chin and round the frill, as in image 1; nothing below the chin.
3. the far front leg: the stubby leg on the far left of image 1, behind the chest, drawn whole from the top of its shoulder (normally hidden behind the body) down to its round foot with soft, round, blunt cream toenails, as in image 1; its top a full, smooth, rounded end with no outline across it.
4. the near front leg: the chubby front leg in the middle of image 1, drawn whole from the top of its shoulder (normally hidden under the chest fluff) down to its big round foot with soft, round, blunt cream toenails, as in image 1; its top a full, smooth, rounded end with no outline across it.
5. the far back leg: the back leg behind the tummy of image 1, mostly hidden there, drawn whole from the top of its thigh down to its round foot with soft, round, blunt cream toenails, shaped like the near back leg; its top a full, smooth, rounded end with no outline across it.
6. the near back leg: the big back leg on the right of image 1, drawn whole from the top of its big round thigh down to its round foot with soft, round, blunt cream toenails, the round thigh with its outline as in image 1.
7. the tail: the short, thick spotted tail with its cream underside, as in image 1, drawn whole from its thick root (normally hidden inside the body) to its rounded tip; its root a soft, smooth edge cut straight across with NO outline.
8. a small sprig of fresh green fern leaves with a short stalk, about as long as the Triceratops's head is wide, in the same drawing style.

Every part is drawn whole, including what is normally hidden behind another part, and each joint end (where it tucks under the body or the head) is a full, smooth, rounded edge. Nothing sharp: no teeth, no pointed claws, every horn soft and blunt. No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a chubby orange Triceratops; image 2 shows the same Triceratops cut into puppet parts, with a blank face. Draw the Triceratops's face pieces as separate stickers on one sheet: the same drawing style, colours and line as in image 1, every piece at the size it has on the Triceratops in image 1, so it fits the blank face in image 2. Its head is turned to the left: its far eye (on the left of image 1, just behind the little nose horn) is smaller and narrower than its near eye (on the right of image 1). In image 1 both eyes look to the left and a little up: each big dark-brown iris sits towards the left of its eye, the white on its right, a white sparkle at its upper left.

Draw each piece on its own, upright, in four tidy rows with wide empty gaps between them, nothing touching:
Row 1, the far eye (the smaller eye, on the LEFT of image 1), six times:
1. as it is in image 1: a tall oval eye, its big dark-brown iris with a white sparkle towards the left, the white on its right, outlined in dark brown.
2. wide open and surprised: bigger and rounder, a warm-brown iris with a dark pupil and a white sparkle, looking the same way.
3. closed in a happy smile: an upward-curving arc, like an upside-down U, with two little lashes.
4. sad: open and round, a soft warm-brown iris with a white sparkle and a thin shine of a welling tear along its bottom rim, looking down and to the left; no lid slanting across it.
5. crying: squeezed shut, a thick lid line as wide as the open eye, curving down at both ends like a little frown, and one small light-blue teardrop just below its outer (left) end.
6. gently closed in sleep: a soft downward-curving line as wide as the open eye, with a few short lashes.
Row 2, the near eye (the bigger eye, on the RIGHT of image 1), the same six in the same order; open, it looks the same way as row 1, to the left, the iris towards the left of the eye; crying, its teardrop below its outer (right) end.
Row 3: 13. the far eyebrow (over the left eye of image 1) as it is in image 1, a short thin dark-brown arch. 14. the same far eyebrow worried: tilted up at its inner (right) end. 15. the near eyebrow (over the right eye of image 1) as it is in image 1, a short thin dark-brown arch. 16. the same near eyebrow worried: tilted up at its inner (left) end.
Row 4, mouths, none with any teeth: 17. the mouth as it is in image 1: a long, thin, closed smiling line running back from the beak, gently curved, curling up into a little smile at its right end. 18. the mouth wide open in a big happy laugh, rounded, under the beak, the inside pink with a little pink tongue, no teeth. 19. the mouth open in a small round 'o', the inside pink. 20. the mouth in a small sad frown. 21. the mouth wide open in a big round yawn, the inside pink with a little tongue, no teeth. 22. the mouth closed and munching: a short wavy closed line with the cheek puffed round, chewing. 23. the mouth sobbing: a small open downturned frown with a little pink inside.

No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows, no face or head around the pieces. Fully transparent background.

animations.description: the Triceratops plods along on its four stubby legs, its big frill nodding gently with each step, then stops.
the Triceratops trots along cheerfully on its four stubby legs, its tail swinging, then stops.
the Triceratops crouches, gives a happy little hop with all four feet off the ground and lands with a soft squash.
the Triceratops nods its big head yes, twice.
the Triceratops shakes its big head no, its frill swinging.
the Triceratops looks one way, then the other, then back.
the Triceratops laughs and laughs, its round tummy bouncing with giggles.
the Triceratops does a happy little dance, stepping from foot to foot, swaying and swinging its tail.
the Triceratops talks, its mouth moving, its big head bobbing a little.
the Triceratops cries, head down, little tears falling, its tummy shaking with sobs.

pause.shows: the Triceratops crying, head down, eyes squeezed shut with tears

animations.description: the Triceratops gives a big yawn, lies down with its legs tucked under it and falls asleep, then wakes up, gets up and smiles.

pause.shows: the Triceratops lying down fast asleep, eyes shut, head resting low

animations.description: the Triceratops shivers and trembles, cold or scared.
the Triceratops lowers its big head and gives a gentle, friendly nudge forward with its frill, twice, then lifts its head with a happy smile.
the Triceratops munches a sprig of fern happily, chewing and chewing until it is all gone, then smiles.
the Triceratops lowers its snout and sniffs the ground, sniff, sniff, then lifts its head with a happy smile.

pause.shows: the Triceratops with its snout down, sniffing the ground

animations.description: the Triceratops wags its short, thick tail happily from side to side.
the Triceratops lifts one front foot and stomps it down, thump, with a little puff of dust, then giggles.
the Triceratops tips its big head down lovingly and nuzzles in, eyes shut happily, all gentle and warm.

pause.shows: the Triceratops with its head tipped down, nuzzling in, eyes shut happily
